title.narrative: WGG- Research and Documentation in Kenya

description.narrative: The strategy of research and documentation is integral to the learning and evidence building agenda of the WGG Consortium and its country-level strategic partners. There are significant programmatic components of the consortium wide joint activities as part of global and regional advocacy efforts.

sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). These organisations exist to bring about transformative change for gender equality and/or the rights of women and girls in developing countries. Their activities include agenda-setting, advocacy, policy dialogue, capacity development, awareness raising and prevention, service provision, conflict-prevention and peacebuilding, research, organising, and alliance and network building

One Training of trainers workshops with 20 participants

KNWD have recently had reflection meetings at the Network level and one-on-one dialogues with project participants at the county level, and we have documented different ways project participants influence at the community level. ‘Confident young girls and women with disabilities,’ is a thread we keep hearing. That now they can speak about things that were spoken of in hushed voices like sexual and gender-based violence against women and girls with disabilities. Now they can attend community gatherings and address these topics. Some champions are taking part in technical working groups on gender and speaking about concerns of women and girls with disabilities. Young champions are starting self-help groups that they are using as advocacy platforms. They are joining other CSOs that are not disability specific and adding their voices on different issues. 19 network champions successfully engaged with community members and duty-bearers across Busia, Meru, Kajiado, Kitui, Nyeri, Isiolo, Nairobi, Kakamega, and Mombasa. They collaborated with state duty bearers, including area chiefs, health practitioners, and both National and County Government officials, as well as nongovernmental institutions such as organizations of persons with disabilities and community leaders and women and girls with disabilities

Under the Kenya Network of Women with disabilities, 20 Champions from 3 Counties were exposed to diverse experiences to strengthen their advocacy skills e.g. leading in marking of the International Day of Persons with Disabilities 2022, documenting violations against girls and women with disabilities . The Champions have also taken part in different trainings like YALI, and DSROI and engaging in SRHR and Political participation events at County levels. The 20 will work with the Network until the end of the WGG project.30 girls and women with disabilities trained in feminist principles, leadership, SGBV, and mentorship through a 3-day training by Women Spaces Africa.10 Young women with disabilities and 10 women working in women's rights organizations were capacitated through the Disability Rights Online institute, DSROI- EA online.
